polozky.nadpis: The Surveyor and Alpha Gal Syndrome
polozky.perex: About forty years ago, I woke up in the middle of the night, itching.
polozky.telo: About forty years ago, I woke up in the middle of the night, itching. Now, it wasn’t a normal itch, it was taking over my entire body. When I turned on the lights, I discovered I was covered with whelps or hives. It was in my scalp, inside my ears and even under my eyelids. I looked like the skin of a strawberry. It continued to get worse and lasted about two hours before subsiding. I told a friend about it. Being light skinned and tending toward red hair, John had sensitive skin and was always peeling or raw somewhere because of the sun. The life of the surveyor. polozky.perex: I love the small computer that fits in my pocket.
polozky.telo: I love the small computer that fits in my pocket. With my smartphone I can conduct hands-free calls, check my calendar to avoid scheduling conflicts, catch up on email between meetings, pay a parking meter from two blocks away. The technology is amazing. This is not to say that new ways are always the best. One big problem with cell phones is that they don’t make a satisfyingly loud and solid bang when I hang up angrily. There definitely was an advantage to those old-fashioned heavy land line phones. The same “old is not always bad” adage applies to surveying.
